summary: The normalized source-to-target kernel is well defined and energy nonincreasing in every case. Its inverse multiplicities, fixed target-dependent denominators, and the sum of overlapping column loads justify the exponential-moment comparison. The ambient-halfspace restriction gives exactly four normalizer factors. The residual-core transport uses the accepted facts with the stated unchanged costs, supports, tilt, cap, marginal, and ambient spaces; the explicit all-cutoff choice of the good set contains every feasible residual cutoff and therefore has mass one. Boundary and degenerate cases satisfy the claims. No mathematical errors or proof gaps were found.
